label: input token m at original positions 1-4
explanation: Fires whenever the input token is m during the original (pre-DEL) phase at positions 1-4, and fires on every such step (precision 1.0). It never fires on m at position 0 or at positions 5 and later, on the delimiter, or on any other token. Magnitude depends on position: highest at t=2 (top examples are m a [m], where m also appeared at t=0), high at t=1, lower at t=3, and weakest at t=4 (about 0.1-0.3 of max). The only misses are 45 tiny activations on copy-phase steps (t=L+2) where the model re-inputs m, holding about 0% of mass.

issues: No refutation found. On the test split the predicate scores precision 1.0, recall 0.9992, F1 0.9996 and mass recall 0.9999, with 0 false positives.

The only misses are 48 test / 45 dev steps, all at t=5 in L=3 sequences, i.e. copy step 2, where an m from original position 1 is fed back in. They are tiny (about 0.03-0.13 of max) and hold 0.0% of the activation mass. They form a systematic class, but a negligible one, and the explanation already describes it accurately.

The magnitude claims hold. Mass share by t is t1 0.329, t2 0.389 (the peak), t3 0.227, t4 0.055. The top examples are all 'm a [m]' at 1.00. Low-quartile examples at t=4 are 0.09-0.21 of max, which fits the claimed 0.1-0.3 range. The feature never fires at t=0 or in original positions 5-8, on the delimiter, or on any input token other than m.
Minor wording point: 'any other token' is right, since m holds 100% of the mass. The label does not overclaim relative to the predicate.
